what_happened: On job 20261023-234149-jcd2 (a prompts job), the user corrected the accepted reading 1. They kept the scope but added a rule. The earlier attempt timed out because the producer ran the full cargo test suite six times, at 9 to 11 minutes each. The user now wants only `cargo test -p athena-context` while editing, and the full suite at most once at the end. The user said the reading did not match what they meant.
cause: The producer has a fixed time deadline but no sense of how long the repo's checks take. Nothing tells it which scoped test command fits the crate it is editing. Nothing limits how often it runs the slow full suite. A small prompt edit can therefore use its whole time budget on repeated 10-minute test runs. The reading, which fixes scope and criteria, also carries no test-running guidance, so the user had to supply that method after the timeout.
prevention: Put the test budget in the harness, not in the prompt. Record the repo's scoped test command per crate and the typical full-suite duration. Run producer test commands through a wrapper that allows the full suite once, or twice at most, and refuses further full runs with a message naming the scoped command. Have the wrapper warn when the remaining time is shorter than one full run. Also keep partial progress when the deadline hits, so a timeout shows what was done and what ate the time.
proposed_request: Make producer runs resistant to timeouts caused by repeated slow test runs. (1) Record in the repo config the scoped test command for each crate (for example `cargo test -p athena-context`) and the typical full-suite duration. (2) Route the producer's test commands through a wrapper that allows the full `cargo test` suite at most once per job, run at the end, and refuses further full runs with a message naming the scoped command to use while editing. (3) Make the wrapper warn when the time left before the producer deadline is less than one full-suite run. (4) When the producer deadline is hit, keep the partial diff and a log of the commands run with their durations. Acceptance: a test shows the wrapper refuses a second full-suite run and allows scoped runs without limit. A test shows the deadline warning appears when time is short. A test shows a timed-out job keeps its partial result and command log. Then re-run job 20261023-234149-jcd2 with its original scope.
